- President Donald Trump signed an executive order on February 18, 2025, aimed at expanding access to in vitro fertilization (IVF) and reducing its costs. The order directs the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy to provide a list of policy recommendations within 90 days to protect IVF access and "aggressively reduce out-of-pocket and health plan costs" for the treatment, which can range from $12,000 to $25,000 per cycle. Requiring insurance companies to cover IVF under the ACA? Classic D.C. bait-and-switch. Government mandates don’t lower costs—they inflate premiums while Big Pharma and insurers pocket the difference. A single IVF cycle costs $15k+ because bureaucrats protect monopolies instead of fostering competition.

Medicare fraud alone wastes $60B annually, yet politicians push more red tape instead of price transparency.

Real reform means breaking pharma’s grip on pricing, auditing hospital billing scams, and letting markets drive innovation—not forcing taxpayers to subsidize a rigged system.

The Health Coverage for IVF Act (H.R. 3480) exemplifies D.C.'s addiction to bloated mandates over real reform. While expanding fertility coverage sounds compassionate, Section 1302(b)(6)(C) forces insurers to fund at least 3 egg retrievals and unlimited embryo transfers per patient—a blank check for Big Fertility clinics charging $20k per cycle.

This isn’t about care—it’s about entrenching a medical-industrial complex that profits from desperation. True reform would audit pharma price gouging on fertility drugs like Follistim ($1,200/vial) and end FDA monopolies blocking cheaper generics.

Instead, this bill layers more bureaucracy onto a broken system, letting insurers pass costs to taxpayers while doing nothing to rein in corporate exploitation of families.
